body:
Metricool: scheduled Sun 2026-10-25 11:00 IG + TikTok
What are AI guardrails? Using AI means accepting risk and responsibility. Put $2k in an AI trading bot with no stop loss and you can lose it all, so set protection measures in any AI process.
guide: AI guardrails are limits you set so an AI agent can only cost you what you chose to risk. You need an AI agent or automation, a clear idea of what it may do, and a way to switch it off.
1. Write down the worst outcome in one sentence, for example "the bot loses the whole £1,500 I put in".
1. Set a hard cap on what the agent can spend or lose, using the limit your platform offers, such as a spending cap, a funded amount, or a stop-loss order on a trading account.
1. Limit the agent's permissions to the minimum, for example read-only access first, and a separate account or API key that only holds the money or data you can afford to lose.

1. Add a human approval step for anything irreversible, such as sending money, emailing customers or deleting records, using a confirmation message in Telegram or a review step in your automation tool.
1. Log every action the agent takes in a spreadsheet, Notion or Supabase table so you can see what it did and why.
1. Add a kill switch, such as a single setting or a revoked API key, that stops the agent immediately.
1. Test with a tiny amount or dummy data for a week before you raise the limits.
Watch out: the post's example was putting $2k into an AI trading bot with no stop loss, which can lose all of it, and the responsibility is yours, not the AI's.

```
You are helping me add guardrails to an AI agent I am about to run. The agent does: <what the agent does, e.g. trades stocks, replies to customer emails>. The tools I use are: <e.g. ChatGPT, Claude Code, n8n, Google Sheets, Telegram, my broker or platform>. The most I am willing to lose or spend is <amount or limit>.
Design and build a simple guardrail layer with these parts:
1. A hard cap on spend, loss or number of actions, enforced outside the AI's own instructions.
2. Minimum permissions, with a separate account or key limited to what I can afford to lose.
3. A human approval step for any irreversible action, sent to <where I want approval requests, e.g. Telegram or email>.
4. An action log in <e.g. Google Sheets or Notion> recording what was done, when and why.
5. A kill switch I can trigger in one step.
6. A test mode that uses dummy data or a tiny amount.
Keep it to the simplest version that works with my tools, and use British spelling. Return the step-by-step setup, any code or workflow needed, and a short checklist for testing the guardrails before I go live. Ask me any questions you need before you start.
```
